verses.text: I'm a rose from Sharon, a lily from the valleys.
Like a lily growing among thorns, that's what my love is like among the other young women.
Like an apple tree in the middle of the woods, that's what my love is like among the other young men. I loved sitting in his shade. His fruit tasted sweet to me.
He took me into the banquet hall. The banner he raised over me was love.
Give me raisins to get my strength back. Refresh me with apples. I'm weak with love.
His left hand cradles my head, and his right arm wraps around me.
Daughters of Jerusalem, swear to me by the gazelles and the does out in the field. Don't stir up love or wake it before it wants to wake.
That's my love's voice! Look, here he comes, leaping over mountains and bounding over hills.
My love is like a gazelle or a young deer. Look, he's standing behind our wall, peeking in through the windows, looking through the lattice.
My love called to me, “Get up, my love, my beautiful one. Come away with me.
Look, winter's over. The rain has stopped and gone.
Flowers are popping up all over the ground. It's time to sing, and you can hear the turtledove in our land.
Green figs are ripening on the tree. The vines are blooming and filling the air with their scent. Get up, my love, my beautiful one. Come away with me.”
My dove, tucked in the cracks of the rock, hiding on the mountainside, let me see your face. Let me hear your voice. Your voice is sweet and your face is lovely.
Catch those foxes for us, the little ones that tear up the vineyards. Our vines are in bloom.
My love is mine and I'm his. He grazes among the lilies.
Till the day cools down and the shadows slip away, turn, my love, and be like a gazelle or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.
